title: Exactness of pullback on module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ any morphism of schemes. The pullback of module objects
$$
f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}
$$
of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] is additive ([def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]) and preserves finite limits and finite colimits. More precisely, both $\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{f^*\Lambda_Y}$ and $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\colon\Mod_{f^*\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ are exact ([def-galois-exact-functor]).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $\mathcal D=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $F=f^*_{\Ab}$, $R=\Lambda_Y$, $S=\Lambda_X$, and $R'=FR$. Abelian sheaves on either small pro-étale site form an abelian category by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. By [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-closed], their sheaf tensor products are closed symmetric monoidal, additive and colimit-preserving in either variable. Thus tensoring on the left by $R,R',S$ preserves finite colimits. The rings $R,S$ are commutative by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The inverse image is strong monoidal by [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], and sends commutative rings to commutative rings by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided], so $R'$ has the requisite commutative transported ring structure. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] to $R$ in $\mathcal C$ and to $R',S$ in $\mathcal D$: all three module categories are abelian. The equalizers and coequalizers required for scalar extension also exist in $\mathcal D$: by [def-sp-abelian] it has kernels and cokernels, and the equalizer, respectively coequalizer, of $a,b$ is the kernel, respectively cokernel, of $a-b$.

source.place: Setting paragraph: abelian and monoidal hypotheses for the three coefficient rings

proof.text: The abelian direct image $T=f_*^{\Ab}$ is additive from its restriction formula [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]: on every object $V$, $T(u+v)_V=(u+v)_{V\times_YX}=u_{V\times_YX}+v_{V\times_YX}$. Use $F\dashv T$ from [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], with unit $\eta$. For parallel sheaf maps $u,v:A\to B$, the adjunction bijection sends $F(u+v)$ to $TF(u+v)\eta_A=\eta_B(u+v)$, and sends $Fu+Fv$ to $T(Fu+Fv)\eta_A=TFu\eta_A+TFv\eta_A=\eta_Bu+\eta_Bv$. The two images coincide by bilinearity, so injectivity gives $F(u+v)=Fu+Fv$. Setting $u=v=0$ and cancelling gives $F0=0$, and then negatives follow. This is additivity in [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor].

source.place: Setting paragraph: expand additivity of the abelian inverse image

proof.text: The functor $F$ is exact by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]. The transport $G=\operatorname{mapMod}(F):\Mod_R(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{R'}(\mathcal D)$ exists by [def-sfb-modobj-transport], whose statement gives the equality $U_{R'}G=FU_R$ on both objects and morphisms. Apply [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] with these $F,G,R,R'$: the additive exactness of $F$ is step 2 and the cited inverse-image lemma; all abelian, tensor-additivity and right-exactness hypotheses were checked in step 1. Hence $G$ is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

source.place: Transport paragraph: apply the general lifting lemma to mapMod

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-alpha-ring-hom], $\alpha_f:R'\to S$ is a morphism of ring objects, for the ring structure on $R'=FR$ transported along the strong monoidal $F$ (the one of step 3), and by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] it is invertible; the inverse of an invertible morphism of ring objects is again one (apply $\alpha_f^{-1}$, resp. $\alpha_f^{-1}\otimes\alpha_f^{-1}$, to the unit and multiplication identities of $\alpha_f$), so $\alpha_f$ is an isomorphism of ring objects. Let $H=\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f^{-1}}:\Mod_{R'}(\mathcal D)\to\Mod_S(\mathcal D)$. The direction follows from $\alpha_f^{-1}:S\to R'$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], $H$ changes only the action and is the identity on underlying objects and morphisms, so $U_SH=\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal D}U_{R'}$. Apply [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] with base functor $\operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal D}$ and module functor $H$, source monoid $R'$ and target monoid $S$. The identity preserves sums and every universal property directly, and the remaining hypotheses are step 1. Thus $H$ is additive and exact.

source.place: Extension of scalars paragraph: exactness of inverse scalar restriction

proof.text: Step 1 verifies all the ambient hypotheses in [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence]: closed braided structure, equalizers and coequalizers, and preservation of colimits by both tensor factors; $R'$ is commutative and step 4 supplies the ring isomorphism. Thus [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso] gives a natural isomorphism $\theta:E=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. For $u,v:M\to N$, naturality yields $E(u+v)=\theta_N^{-1}H(u+v)\theta_M=\theta_N^{-1}(Hu+Hv)\theta_M=Eu+Ev$. For a finite diagram $D$ and a limiting cone $c$ with vertex $A$, a cone $b_j:B\to E(D_j)$ becomes the cone $\theta_{D_j}b_j$ over $HD$. Since $Hc$ is limiting, it has a unique factorization $t:B\to HA$. The map $\theta_A^{-1}t$ is the unique factorization through $Ec$, by naturality and invertibility of $\theta$. This proves finite-limit preservation by $E$. For a cocone $b_j:E(D_j)\to B$, compose with $\theta_{D_j}^{-1}$, factor uniquely through $HA$ using the colimit property of $Hc$, and compose the resulting map $HA\to B$ with $\theta_A$. This proves finite-colimit preservation. Hence $E$ is additive and exact.

source.place: Extension of scalars paragraph, final sentence: expand invariance under natural isomorphism

proof.text: The pullback in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] is exactly $E\circ G$. For parallel module maps $u,v$, $(EG)(u+v)=E(Gu+Gv)=EGu+EGv$. If $c$ is a limiting cone for a finite diagram, $Gc$ is limiting by step 3 and $E(Gc)$ is limiting by step 5; the same argument for colimiting cocones proves finite-colimit preservation. Thus the composite is additive and exact in the sense of [def-galois-exact-functor], as are both factors by steps 3 and 5. This proves every assertion without any finiteness or characteristic condition on $\Lambda$.
